description.fun: Diglett always seems to be buried up to its nose, and sunlight heats its blood and leaves it weak, so it stays underground, leaving perfectly tilled soil behind it. Some farmers welcome it for that, while others call it a pest for eating their vegetables. It's modelled on the moles of Whac-A-Mole, and its Japanese name, Digda, nods to the arcade game Dig Dug.
description.guide: A tiny Ground Pokémon that lives underground with only its head showing. It digs through soil at a shallow depth, eating roots and leaving the earth tilled, and avoids sunlight. It evolves into Dugtrio, and its Alolan form has golden steel whiskers.
description.tagline: A little mole that tills the fields it raids

names.ja: アローラ ディグダ

description.fun: Living in Alola's iron-rich volcanic soil gave it three fine golden whiskers made of steel, which work as sensors so it can check its surroundings without surfacing. They stand up when it's angry, swing when it's happy and droop when it's sad.

Dugtrio is Diglett triplets sharing one body, though nobody has ever seen it, since it never leaves the ground. The three heads think the same thoughts and work together, bobbing to loosen the soil, though they occasionally squabble over who eats first. It tunnels at 100 km/h as deep as 100 km, setting off tremors as it goes.
description.guide: The evolution of Diglett: three Diglett heads sharing one body that stays buried underground. It can tunnel at great speed and depth, causing tremors, and its digging keeps soil good for farming. Its Alolan form has three heads of long golden steel hair.
description.tagline: Three heads, and a body nobody's ever seen

names.ja: アローラ ダグトリオ

description.fun: Each head sports a mop of golden hair made of thin, heavy strands of steel. Alolans revere it as a feminine deity of the earth, believe taking its hairs brings bad luck, and say a crowd of them popping up warns of an eruption.
